name: Fari'ah bint Tarif
bio: Fari'ah bint Tarif was the sister of al-Walid ibn Tarif al-Shaybani, a Kharijite rebel who rose against the caliph Harun al-Rashid and was killed in battle by the Abbasid commander Yazid ibn Mazyad.

Her dirge for her brother is among the most famous elegies by an Arab woman. It is the only poem attributed to her that is widely known, and it is preserved in the classical anthologies of Arabic verse.

poems.title: Dirge for Her Brother al-Walid
poems.author: Fari'ah bint Tarif
poems.collection: Translations of Eastern Poetry and Prose (1922)
poems.text:
At Tallu Nuhaka stands the cairn of a grave set high
As though on a mountain-peak o'ertopping the mountains,
A grave that doth hold renown most ancient and chieftainhood
And courage heroical and judgment unshaken.
But why bud ye, O ye trees of Khabur, with leaves afresh?
Methinks, ye have never mourned Tarif's son, my brother.
He liked not of food but that he gained in the fear of God,
Of wealth only what was won by good swords and lances;
Nor aught would he prize and keep but many a hardy mare
Sleek-coated, well-used to charge thro' ranks of the battle.
And now 'tis as though with us thou ne'er hadst been present here,
Or ta'en 'gainst our foes a stand not soon to be yielded;
Or ever done on, for sake of plunging in loathly fray,
A hauberk of mail amongst dark-glittering horsemen;
Or striven on a field of War, when big is her womb with woe
And keen tawny-shafted pikes have pricked her to fury.
The comrade of Bounty he, his life long: him Bounty loved,
And since he is dead, no more loves Bounty a comrade.
We lost thee as Youth, once lost, returns not; and fain had we
Redeemed thee with thousands of the lives of our bravest.
